findings.body:
**Do not dispatch a paid judge from `--triage-dry-run`.**

With a configured rollout and a pending finding, `phase()` calls the supplied judge even when `dry_run=True`. The callback creates scan artifacts at Lines 767–768 and can dispatch a provider at Line 785. This path also bypasses `service.lock` and the normal paid admission checks. For a dry run, report which candidates would need judgment without calling the live judge. Keep provider dispatch on the admitted live path.
findings.title: Do not dispatch a paid judge from `--triage-dry-run`.

findings.body:
**Reject conflicting selectors before the dry-run branch.**

With repair enabled, `--recover-job ID --triage-dry-run` takes the early return at Lines 1237–1243. It never reaches this conflict check. Validate selector combinations before routing to any operation, and keep standalone `--triage-dry-run` valid.
findings.title: Reject conflicting selectors before the dry-run branch.

findings.body:
**Do not let one malformed result block the drain.**

If a queued major job still has the malformed `result.json` exercised at Line 779 of `test_repair_bounded.py`, `pending()` raises while the drain sorts items. No item reaches `drain_items()`, including unrelated jobs with valid inputs. Preserve the malformed artifact for tick reconciliation, but exclude that job from dispatch in both the priority check and item processing. Keep the existing distinction between a missing result and a valid terminal result.
findings.title: Do not let one malformed result block the drain.

findings.body:
**Return JSON on argument errors and operation failures.**

An unknown flag makes `parse_args()` exit before `main()` writes a result. A selected job that has been removed raises from `select_job()` and also leaves stdout empty. Route these failures through the result writer. Preserve exit code `2` for usage errors and `1` for thrown operation errors. As per coding guidelines, “Every operation invocation writes machine-readable JSON to stdout and human narration to stderr, never mixed.”
findings.title: Return JSON on argument errors and operation failures.

findings.body:
**Emit one JSON artifact when a drain runs triage.**

When configured triage completes, this line writes the triage result. The automatic drain then writes `{"status":"drained"}` through `main()`. A consumer cannot parse the two objects as one document. Return the triage result to `run()` and let `main()` write it once, either as the dry-run result or as part of the drain result. As per coding guidelines, “stdout is still exactly one JSON artifact.”
findings.title: Emit one JSON artifact when a drain runs triage.

findings.body:
**Use a fresh checkout for each fallback fixer.**

If the first fixer leaves an ignored file and returns `rate-limit`, `git reset --hard` and `git clean -fd` leave that file in the checkout. The next provider starts in the same checkout and can observe the first fixer's state. Use a fresh checkout at `baseline` for the fallback and preserve the previous checkout for investigation. As per coding guidelines, “Each per-file or per-job worker is a fresh, isolated invocation; context never leaks between workers.” The supplied `retain()` implementation also excludes ignored files.
findings.title: Use a fresh checkout for each fallback fixer.

findings.body:
**Honor the cooldown when retrying a non-CQ judge.**

If a Codex or Paseo judge returns `rate-limit`, `defer()` writes a global pause and a future `retry_after`. With fallback models configured, a ready CQ role makes `dispatch_paused()` ignore that pause at Line 272. `process()` then ignores `retry_after` at Line 372, but this branch sends the retry to the same judge without checking its cooldown. Apply fallback admission to the lane being dispatched. Let a ready CQ fallback proceed without reopening a rate-limited non-CQ lane.
findings.title: Honor the cooldown when retrying a non-CQ judge.

findings.body:
**Recompute the triage budget after the context scan.**

If `phase()` has two seconds left when it calls `judge()` and the scan takes three seconds, this line still gives the provider two seconds. The provider can start after the phase deadline. Record the deadline at callback entry, then recompute the time left immediately before dispatch. If no time remains, return a deadline stop without invoking the provider. The supplied `phase()` implementation measures `remaining` before it calls this callback.
findings.title: Recompute the triage budget after the context scan.
